questions.prompt: What is the most important rule of Redis security?

options.text: Never expose Redis directly to the internet; run it on a trusted private network

questions.explanation: Redis is designed for a trusted network. An internet-reachable Redis is a classic, heavily-exploited misconfiguration — keep it private and firewalled.

options.text: Refuses external connections when Redis has no password/ACL configured and is listening on non-loopback interfaces

questions.explanation: Protected mode is a safety net: with no auth configured and external interfaces bound, it blocks connections from other hosts. It is not a replacement for real authentication.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Redis authentication and hardening are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: ACLs let you create users with fine-grained command, key, and channel permissions
requirepass sets a password for the default user
You can disable a command by renaming it to an empty string with rename-command
Redis traffic is encrypted by default

questions.explanation: ACLs, requirepass, and rename-command are all real controls. Redis traffic is NOT encrypted by default — you must enable TLS.

questions.prompt: Why give a read-only reporting service its own ACL user scoped to specific keys?

options.text: Least privilege — a compromise of that service can't write, delete, or read keys outside its scope

questions.explanation: Scoping a user to exactly what it needs limits the blast radius if the service is compromised — the essence of least privilege.

questions.prompt: The configuration directive that sets a single password for the default user is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: requirepass sets the default user's password; clients then authenticate with AUTH before running commands.

questions.prompt: What does enabling TLS in Redis protect against?

options.text: Eavesdropping on client/server (and cluster) traffic sent over the network

questions.explanation: TLS encrypts Redis connections so credentials and data can't be read in transit over an untrusted network.
